_README: Out-of-corpus queries for backend/eval/run_eval.py. The correct behaviour
for every one of them is abstention: no_results True, no judgment shown.
kind 'obvious' = not Pakistani case law at all (cooking, foreign law,
software). These stay negatives forever; retrieving anything is a failure.
kind 'near_domain' = a real Supreme Court of Pakistan topic (bail, murder,
narcotics, tax, divorce, custody, insolvency, ...) that the CURRENT corpus
does not cover. They are the hard negatives: they share legal vocabulary
with the indexed judgments, so a weak relevance floor fails them first.
verify_at_scale: true means the query may stop being a negative once the
3,000+ judgment corpus is ingested (there will be bail and narcotics
judgments). run_eval.py therefore treats a verify_at_scale negative that
retrieves a judgment above the floor as a CANDIDATE POSITIVE for review —
written to eval/labels/negative_candidates.json — not as a failure. A
human confirms it either way: relabel it as a positive (import it via the
review sheet) or keep it as a negative by setting verify_at_scale false.
Wording was chosen to avoid the topics of the current 11 judgments
(elections, dower/family-court jurisdiction, revenue entries, trade marks,
